name: HDFC Bank Ltd
title: HDFC Bank Ltd - 500180 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 call shows CASA and margin pressure persisting with no near-term fix; management pins recovery on FCNR(B) flows and acquisition quality, but gave no numeric guidance and deferred margin and CEO-reappointment answers.

triggers.label: Cost of funds flat QoQ, down ~40-50bp YoY
triggers.quote: it's about call it 40, 50 basis points, 40 basis points or so year-to-year

triggers.label: CASA ratio fell to 34%, peers ~40%
triggers.quote: that sharp decline in CASA down to 34%. I know there are several reasons for it. All of your peers are at 40%

triggers.label: Corporate/wholesale advances growing ~18%
triggers.quote: We've seen that grow at about 18% and this is continuing

triggers.label: Management refuses FCNR(B) number
triggers.quote: Whilst demand is there, we just don't want to commit any number.

guidance.quote: We do think that in the longer term that the profit growth should be at or above the balance sheet growth.

guidance.value: Return toward ~38% (pre/post-merger level), medium to long term
guidance.quote: the endeavor and our vision is to reach to somewhere near the pre-merger levels or just around the time of the merger, which was around 38.

red_flags.quote: it shows 9.8% profit growth, yes. But 9.8% profit growth is still lower than the overall balance sheet growth

summary.headline: HDFC Bank Q1 FY27 reported profit growth of 5% YoY (9.8% adjusted); CASA ratio at 34%, cost of funds flat QoQ and down ~40-50 bps YoY.
summary.overview: Management described a tough four months but said deposit growth was better than historical Q1 trends and market share gains continued. Reported PAT rose 5% YoY, which management said was 9.8% after adjusting for prior-year one-offs (HDB gains, floating and contingent provisions). Management guided that margins will not change quickly, with the non-retail cost of funds and borrowing mix (~11%) as the main levers. The call also covered the FCNR (B) window, ECLGS 5.0 disbursements of about INR 14,000 crore, the upcoming ECL transition on 1 April 2027, and the appointment of a new part-time Chairman, Rajiv Kumar. The MD reappointment and additional whole-time director appointments remain work in progress with no timeline given.

financial_highlights.change: Management says adjusted growth is 9.8% after excluding HDB gains and provisions in the prior year

financial_highlights.value: Flat QoQ (within a couple of bps); down about 40-50 bps YoY

financial_highlights.change: Down from earlier levels; industry around 5-6%
Analyst cited 34%; management target is around 38% (post-merger level)

financial_highlights.value: Close to INR 14,000 crore as of 30 June

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail is 52% of advances. Management said wheels, unsecured and mortgage disbursements grew strongly YoY, while the unsecured book growth remains in single digits. Gold loans and dukandar micro loans are described as growing.

segments.name: MSME / business banking
segments.commentary: Business banking, the largest MSME component, grew 22.3% YoY, and ECLGS 5.0 disbursements reached about INR 14,000 crore by 30 June.

segments.name: Corporate and wholesale
segments.commentary: Corporate and wholesale advances grew about 18%. Management said corporate spreads remain thin and it is being selective.

guidance_outlook: Margins: cost of funds is the main lever with a possible 40-50 bps change, but management said it will not change in a hurry. It does not expect margins to bottom quarter to quarter and sees a better full-year position.
Borrowings: management does not expect the borrowing mix to settle at 8-9%, and expects maturity and growth to bring it down over time.
Profit growth: management expects profit growth at or above balance sheet growth over the longer term, but not on a quarterly basis.
FCNR (B): documentation is complete with counterparty banks; management expects milestones in July-September and aims for a significant share of the system, similar to 2014-15.
ECL: transition effective 1 April 2027. Management expects some increase in credit cost from higher floors (unsecured stage 1 at 1%, stage 2 at 5%) but nothing material.
Customer acquisition: management expects a step-up in acquisition quality and value over the next nine months and in savings account growth over one to three years.
capex_capacity: Branch network is about 9,700 branches, with about 40% under five years old.
Investment in distribution will be slightly muted going forward, while technology spending continues, including AI and security.
Management expects efficiency gains from faster turnaround times over the next two to three years.
Some GenAI lighthouse programmes are expected to go into production during the year.
demand_pricing: Corporate spreads remain very thin amid intense competition; the bank is selective and pursues holistic primary relationships.
Granular deposit rates are reasonably stable, while non-granular (bulk) deposit rates remain elevated.
System liquidity averaged about INR 2.08 trillion in the recent quarter, with a peak of INR 5.5 trillion and a trough of negative INR 0.43 trillion.
Household deposit growth is among the lowest of the deposit categories.
Management says the bank gained market share on a stock and incremental basis in deposits. Its FY26 CASA growth was 9.5-10%, but it still gained share.
Time deposits are a major opportunity, with only 14% of customers holding them.

qa_highlights.question: Have margins bottomed out, and what are the headwinds and tailwinds, including FCNR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost of funds is the main opportunity, with a possible 40-50 bps change that will not happen quickly. It would not call a quarterly bottom but expects a better full year.

qa_highlights.question: Have the branch additions from FY22-23 scaled as expected, and what would restore SA market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-branch deposits are about INR 330 crore vs INR 266 crore in FY23. Management attributed the SA share slowdown to household deposit weakness and to tighter acquisition guardrails against mule accounts over FY24-26, and expects healthier SA growth over one to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CASA ratio return to 40% and what is the CEO reappointment status?
qa_highlights.answer: The vision is to return to around 38%, the post-merger level, over the medium to long term. Management said the CASA-rate correlation is weaker, with growth to come from unit economics. On reappointment, the NRC and Board are working on it, with an announcement to follow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bond maturity profile and the rate benefit from replacing borrowings with deposits?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 40,000-50,000 crore of borrowings mature over the next couple of years. Replacing them with time deposits gives about 100-125 bps benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-time ECL transition impact and the ongoing credit cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current provisions are adequate for transition. Ongoing credit cost will rise because of higher floors, but the impact is not expected to be material, and contingent provisions cover it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for growth and PCR after the ECL transition?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate and wholesale grew about 18%, business banking 22.3% and mortgage disbursements about 14%. Coverage was 66% headline, and management said PCR is formula-driven and tied to book mix.

risks_watch: CASA ratio at 34% vs a target of about 38%; wholesale deposit share has risen to about 20%.
Non-granular deposit rates remain elevated and liquidity volatility is high.
Retail unsecured book growth remains in single digits, with cards book growth at 2.3%.
ECL transition from 1 April 2027 will raise standard-asset provisions via higher floors.
Leadership: MD reappointment is pending, and additional whole-time directors are expected but not yet appointed.
El Nino and West Asia geopolitical risks; management said El Nino impact will show in Q3 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise, growth and the FCNR opportunity, but evasive on specific margin, CASA and leadership timelines, which management repeatedly deferred to the full year or to later announcements.
key_quotes: Advances, as we had envisioned a while ago, I think we are on the verge of pressing the pedal.

So, the thought process that we have as Srini did mention is that we are probably now after putting in our guardrails in terms of what kind of customers need to come in into the institution from an acquisition perspective, I think we are now ready to press the pedal.
The industry is more like a 5% or a 6%, right?
But 9.8% profit growth is still lower than the overall balance sheet growth correct.

growth.why: Management guides only to longer-term profit growth at or above balance sheet growth and a CASA return toward ~38% over the medium to long term, with no quantified near-term revenue guidance; reported PAT rose 5% YoY (9.8% adjusted), and no capacity additions were discussed beyond the existing ~9,700-branch network.

mgmt.note: New part-time Chairman Rajiv Kumar appointed; MD reappointment and additional whole-time director appointments remain work in progress with no timeline given.
